title: Batata harra (Lebanese spicy garlic and coriander potatoes)

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for 5 to 6 minutes until just tender, then drain and let them steam dry.
Fry them in about 1 cm of hot oil in batches until golden and crisp, and drain.
Pour off most of the oil and stir the garlic and chilli in the pan for 30 seconds without browning.
Return the potatoes with the coriander and lemon juice and toss for a minute.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Fattoush (Lebanese bread and vegetable salad with sumac)

ingredients.name: fresh mint and flat-leaf parsley, chopped

steps: Toast or fry the torn pita until deep golden and crisp, and set aside to cool.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, sumac, pomegranate molasses and salt into a dressing.
Combine the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, radishes, spring onions and herbs in a large bowl.
Pour over the dressing and toss gently.
Add the crisp bread just before serving so it stays crunchy, and finish with a dusting of sumac.

title: Hrisseh (Lebanese wheat and chicken porridge)

ingredients.name: hulled wheat berries (or pearled wheat/spelt), soaked overnight

steps: Put the drained wheat, chicken, onion and cinnamon stick in a heavy pot with the water and bring to the boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer very gently for about 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally, adding hot water if it gets too dry.
Remove the chicken, discard the skin and bones, and shred the meat.
Return the meat to the pot, season with salt, and beat the mixture vigorously with a wooden spoon or masher for about 10 minutes until it becomes a smooth, thick, sticky porridge.
Serve in shallow bowls, with a well in the centre filled with melted butter and sprinkled with ground cinnamon.

title: Hummus (Lebanese chickpea and tahini dip)

ingredients.name: pinch of paprika and chopped parsley, for serving

steps: If using dried chickpeas, soak them overnight, then boil them with a pinch of baking soda for about 1.5 hours until very soft, and cool.
Blend the tahini with the lemon juice and garlic for a minute until pale and thick.
Add the chickpeas, salt and the ice-cold water gradually, blending for 3 to 4 minutes until very smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust the lemon, salt and garlic.
Spread on a plate, make a hollow, fill with olive oil, and dust with paprika and parsley. Serve with warm pita.

title: Kibbeh bil sanieh (Lebanese baked kibbeh)
steps: Fry the chopped onion in a spoonful of the butter until soft, add the ground lamb and brown it, then add the pine nuts, a pinch of allspice, salt and pepper. Cool the filling.
Process the lean lamb with the quartered onion, salt, allspice and cinnamon into a smooth paste, adding a little iced water as needed.
Mix the paste with the bulgur and knead well until it is a smooth, cohesive dough.
Press half the kibbeh into the base of a greased 25 cm baking dish with wet hands, spread the filling over it, and cover with the remaining kibbeh, smoothing the top.
Score the top into diamonds, make a hole in the centre of each, and pour the melted butter over the surface.
Bake at 200 C for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and firm, and serve hot with yogurt.

title: Kousa mahshi (Lebanese stuffed courgettes in tomato sauce)
steps: Trim the courgettes and hollow out each one with a corer or long spoon, leaving a wall of about 5 mm and keeping the end closed.
Mix the lamb, rice, onion, allspice, cinnamon, oil, salt and pepper for the filling.
Fill each courgette about two-thirds full, leaving room for the rice to expand.
Lay them snugly in a wide pot in a single layer and pour over the tomatoes mixed with the tomato paste, garlic, mint and 300 ml of water.
Place a plate on top to hold them down, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 40 to 45 minutes until tender.
Stir the lemon juice into the sauce and serve hot.

title: Layali lubnan (Lebanese semolina pudding with cream)

ingredients.name: thick cream (ashta, clotted cream or whipped cream with a little mascarpone)

steps: Make a syrup by simmering the 100 g sugar and water for 8 minutes, then adding the rose water and cooling.
Whisk the milk, semolina, cornflour and sugar together in a pot and heat gently, stirring constantly, until thick and bubbling.
Stir in the orange blossom water and pour into a shallow dish or small glasses, smoothing the top.
Let it cool, then chill until firm, about 2 hours.
Spread the cream over the set pudding and top with the ground pistachios.
Drizzle with the cool syrup just before serving.

title: Ma'amoul (Lebanese date and walnut semolina cookies)

ingredients.name: date paste, for a date filling (optional alternative)

steps: Stir the semolina, flour and sugar together, pour in the melted butter and rub it in with your fingertips. Cover and rest for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Work in the milk, orange blossom water and rose water until the dough holds together when squeezed.
Mix the walnuts with the filling sugar and cinnamon, or work the date paste until soft.
Take a walnut-sized piece of dough, make a cup, fill with a teaspoon of filling, and close it. Press into a ma'amoul mould or shape by hand and mark with a fork.
Bake on a lined tray at 180 C for 15 to 20 minutes until set but still pale.
Cool completely and dust the walnut ones with icing sugar.

title: Malfouf salad (Lebanese cabbage, lemon and mint salad)
steps: Shred the cabbage as finely as possible and place it in a large bowl.
Sprinkle with salt and rub the cabbage with your hands for a minute to soften it.
Whisk together the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil and dried mint.
Pour the dressing over the cabbage and toss well.
Let it sit for 15 minutes so the flavours mingle, then serve with grilled meats or as part of a mezze.

title: Manakish (Lebanese za'atar flatbread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the oil and warm water, and knead for about 8 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and let it rise for 1 hour until doubled, then divide into 6 balls and rest for 15 minutes.
Stir the za'atar into the olive oil to make a spreadable paste.
Roll each ball into a round about 15 cm across, press in dimples with your fingertips, and spread with the za'atar paste, leaving a border.
Bake on a very hot tray or stone at 230 C for 8 to 10 minutes until puffed and golden at the edges.
Serve warm for breakfast with tomatoes, cucumber, olives and fresh mint.

title: Meghli (Lebanese spiced rice pudding for celebrations)

ingredients.name: mixed chopped almonds, pistachios and walnuts, for topping

steps: Whisk the rice flour with 250 ml of the cold water until smooth, then whisk in the remaining water in a pot.
Add the sugar and spices and bring to the boil over medium heat, stirring constantly so no lumps form.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until thickened to the consistency of a loose custard.
Pour into small bowls and let cool, then chill for at least 3 hours until set.
Top with the nuts and coconut before serving.

title: Muhallebi (Lebanese milk pudding with rose water and pistachios)
steps: Mix the cornflour with 200 ml of the cold milk until smooth.
Heat the rest of the milk with the sugar until it is steaming but not boiling.
Whisk in the cornflour mixture and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the pudding thickens and just starts to bubble, about 8 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the orange blossom water and rose water.
Pour into small bowls and chill for at least 3 hours.
Top with ground pistachios before serving.

title: Raheb salad (Lebanese monk's salad of smoked aubergine)
steps: Char the aubergines whole over a gas flame, under a hot grill or in a very hot oven for 20 to 30 minutes until the skins blacken and the flesh collapses.
Cool them in a covered bowl, then peel off the skins and drain off the juices.
Chop the flesh roughly and mix it with the tomatoes, onion, parsley and garlic.
Dress with lemon juice, olive oil, pomegranate molasses and salt.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve at room temperature with pita.

title: Sfiha (Lebanese open lamb pies)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the oil and warm water and knead into a soft dough. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Mix the lamb with the onion, tomato, pomegranate molasses, allspice, salt and pepper.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll or press each into a small round about 10 cm across.
Spread a spoonful of topping over each round, leaving the edge bare, and press in a few pine nuts.
Bake on trays at 230 C for 10 to 12 minutes until the dough is golden and the meat is cooked through.
Serve warm with yogurt and lemon wedges.

title: Sfouf (Lebanese turmeric and almond semolina cake)
steps: Grease a 23 cm baking tin with the tahini, spreading it thinly over the base and sides.
Whisk the semolina, flour, sugar, turmeric, baking powder and aniseed together in a bowl.
Stir in the oil and milk until you have a smooth batter and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Pour the batter into the tin and scatter the pine nuts or almonds over the top.
Bake at 180 C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin and cut into diamond-shaped pieces.

title: Shish taouk (Lebanese yogurt and garlic marinated chicken skewers)

ingredients.name: boneless chicken breast or thigh, cut into 3 cm cubes

steps: Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, tomato paste, garlic, oil, paprika, allspice and salt into a marinade.
Add the chicken and turn to coat, then cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, leaving small gaps between pieces.
Grill over medium-hot coals or under a grill for 12 to 15 minutes, turning often, until lightly charred and cooked through.
Serve with garlic sauce, pickles, fries and flatbread, or in a wrap.

title: Tabbouleh (Lebanese parsley and bulgur salad)

ingredients.name: flat-leaf parsley leaves, very finely chopped (about 3 large bunches)

steps: Soak the bulgur in the lemon juice for 15 minutes, or until it has absorbed the juice and softened.
Wash the parsley and mint very well and dry them thoroughly, then chop them as finely as you can with a sharp knife.
Dice the tomatoes and let them drain briefly in a sieve so the salad does not turn watery.
Combine the herbs, tomatoes, spring onions and soaked bulgur in a bowl.
Dress with olive oil, allspice, salt and pepper, tossing just before serving, and serve with crisp romaine leaves for scooping.

title: Znoud el-sit (Lebanese cream-filled filo rolls)

ingredients.name: filo pastry sheets, cut in half

steps: Whisk the milk, cornflour and sugar over medium heat until it thickens into a custard, stir in the cream and rose water, and cool completely.
Simmer the syrup sugar and water for 8 minutes with a squeeze of lemon and let it cool.
Spoon a line of cream along the short edge of each half-sheet of filo, fold in the sides, and roll it up into a tight cigar, sealing the end with a dab of water.
Fry the rolls in 3 to 4 cm of oil at 170 C, turning, for 1 to 2 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain, then dip or drizzle with the cool syrup and sprinkle with pistachios. Eat the same day.
